paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. Two blind men cry out for mercy, and Jesus asks them a question: "Do you believe that I am able to do this?" They say, "Yes, Lord," and He tells them, "According to your faith will it be done to you." (Matthew 9:28-29) They didn't bring a plan or a résumé. They brought trust, and that's what Jesus asked about.

Now watch what happens after. Jesus warns them sternly, "See that no one finds out about this!" and they go out and spread the news throughout the land anyway. (Matthew 9:30-31) I'm not here to pile on those two. I think they were so full of joy they couldn't hold it in, and I know that feeling. It tells me that when Jesus does something in your life, it's hard to stay quiet about it.

Then comes the part to sit with. The crowds see a mute man start to speak and say, "Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!" But the Pharisees, a group of Jewish religious leaders, say, "It is by the prince of demons that He drives out demons." (Matthew 9:33-34) Same Jesus, same miracle, two very different responses. So here's my question for you, baker: when you see Jesus at work, will you cry out, "Have mercy on us," and trust Him like those two men did?
